([[Gig Harbor, Washington]]) | college = * [[Oregon State Beavers men's basketball|Oregon State]] (2016–2017) * [[UC Santa Barbara Gauchos men's basketball|UC Santa Barbara]] (2018–2021) | draft_year = 2021 | career_start = 2021 | years1 = {{nbay|2021|full=y}} | team1 = [[Dallas Mavericks]] | years2 = [[2021–22 NBA G League season|2021–2022]] | team2 = →[[Texas Legends]] | years3 = [[2022–23 NBA G League season|2022–2023]] | team3 = [[Santa Cruz Warriors]] | years4 = 2023 | team4 = [[Otago Nuggets]] | years5 = 2024–2025 | team5 = [[Pelita Jaya Basketball Club|Pelita Jaya]] | years6 = 2025 | team6 = [[Illawarra Hawks]] | years7 = [[2025–26 NBA G League season|2025]]–present | team7 = [[Valley Suns]] | highlights = *[[All-IBL Indonesian Team|All-IBL Second Team]] ([[2025 IBL Indonesia|2025]]) * [[Indonesian Basketball League|IBL]] All-Star ([[2025 IBL Indonesia|2025]]) * Honorable Mention [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] – [[Associated Press|AP]] ([[2021 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|2021]]) * [[Big West Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Big West Player of the Year]] (2021) * First-team All-[[Big West Conference|Big West]] (2021) * [[Big West Conference men's basketball tournament|Big West tournament]] MVP ([[2021 Big West Conference men's basketball tournament|2021]]) * [[Washington Mr. Basketball]] (2016) }} '''JaQuori McLaughlin''' (born January 29, 1998) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Valley Suns]] of the [[NBA G League]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Oregon State Beavers men's basketball|Oregon State Beavers]] and the [[UC Santa Barbara Gauchos men's basketball|UC Santa Barbara Gauchos]]. ==Early life== McLaughlin attended [[Peninsula High School (Washington)|Peninsula High School]] in [[Gig Harbor, Washington]]. He averaged 19.3 points, 9.1 assists and 5.5 steals per game as a senior and was named [[Washington Mr. Basketball]]. McLaughlin left as the school's all-time leader in points, assists and three-pointers.{{cite web |last1=Cotterill |first1=TJ |title=Mr. Basketball: JaQuori McLaughlin is 'gold standard' of Peninsula basketball |url=https://www.thenewstribune.com/sports/high-school/article61911177.html |website=[[The News Tribune]] |access-date=February 19, 2021 |date=February 22, 2016}} He had originally committed to playing college basketball for [[Oregon State Beavers men's basketball|Oregon State]] before switching his commitment to [[Washington Huskies men's basketball|Washington]]. He later recommitted to Oregon State over offers from [[Utah Utes men's basketball|Utah]] and [[Wisconsin Badgers men's basketball|Wisconsin]].{{cite web |last1=Nemec |first1=Andrew |title=JaQuori McLaughlin, 4-star PG, commits to Oregon State Beavers over Utah, Wisconsin |url=https://www.oregonlive.com/recruiting/2015/09/jaquori_mclaughlin_4-star_pg_c.html |website=[[The Oregonian]] |access-date=February 19, 2021 |date=September 25, 2015}} ==College career== As a freshman at Oregon State, McLaughlin averaged 10.5 points and 3.3 assists per game. He set a program freshman record with 58 three-pointers.{{cite web |last1=Sowa |first1=Jesse |title=OSU men's basketball: McLaughlin leaves program |url=https://www.gazettetimes.com/sports/beavers-sports/basketball/osu-mens-basketball-mclaughlin-leaves-program/article_0a446f0e-ffff-5e3e-9beb-bb0a0f30577e.html |website=[[Corvallis Gazette-Times]] |access-date=February 19, 2021 |date=December 1, 2017}} Before his second year, McLaughlin began suffering from [[post-traumatic stress disorder]] after witnessing a [[2017 Barcelona attacks|terrorist attack]] during his team's summer trip to Spain. Six games into the season, he left the team.{{cite web |last1=Patton |first1=Mark |title=JaQuori McLaughlin returns to Oregon State, but happy to have landed at UCSB |url=https://newspress.com/patton-jaquori-mclaughlin-returns-to-oregon-state-but-happy-to-have-landed-at-ucsb/ |website=[[Santa Barbara News-Press]] |access-date=February 19, 2021 |date=November 20, 2019 |archive-date=March 2, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210302150842/https://newspress.com/patton-jaquori-mclaughlin-returns-to-oregon-state-but-happy-to-have-landed-at-ucsb/ |url-status=dead }} McLaughlin was granted a [[Redshirt (college sports)|redshirt]] and transferred to [[UC Santa Barbara Gauchos men's basketball|UC Santa Barbara]].{{cite web |last1=Manley |first1=Jon |title=After transferring from Oregon State, Peninsula grad McLaughlin feeling at home at UC Santa Barbara |url=https://www.thenewstribune.com/news/local/community/gateway/g-sports/article223265370.html |website=[[The News Tribune]] |access-date=February 19, 2021 |date=December 22, 2018}} He averaged 10.3 points and 3.2 assists per game as a sophomore. In his junior season, he averaged 13.4 points and 4.1 assists per game. McLaughlin was named to the All-[[Big West Conference|Big West]] Honorable Mention.{{cite web |last1=Klan |first1=Mike |title=McLaughlin relishes leadership role for Gauchos |url=https://keyt.com/sports/college-sports/2020/10/20/mclaughlin-relishes-leadership-role-for-gauchos/ |publisher=[[KEYT-TV]] |access-date=February 19, 2021 |date=October 20, 2020}} As a senior, he averaged 16 points, 5.2 assists, 3.5 rebounds and 1.5 steals per game, helping UC Santa Barbara win the Big West regular season and tournament title. McLaughlin was named [[Big West Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Big West Player of the Year]] as well as Big West tournament MVP. Following the season, McLaughlin declared for the [[2021 NBA draft]] forgoing his extra season of eligibility.{{cite news |last1=Smith |first1=Lauren |title=UC Santa Barbara guard JaQuori McLaughlin, a Peninsula product, declares for NBA Draft |url=https://www.thenewstribune.com/sports/high-school/article250895144.html |access-date=June 20, 2021 |work=[[The News Tribune]] |date=April 24, 2021}} ==Professional career== ===Dallas Mavericks (2021–2022)=== After going undrafted in the [[2021 NBA draft]], McLaughlin played for the [[Golden State Warriors]] in the [[2021 NBA Summer League|NBA Summer League]].{{cite web|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/player/JaQuori-McLaughlin/Summary/85624|title=JaQuori McLaughlin|work=realgm.com|access-date=March 31, 2023}} On September 4, 2021, he signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Dallas Mavericks]]. Under the terms of the deal, he split time between the Mavs and their [[NBA G League]] affiliate, the [[Texas Legends]].{{cite web|first=Eddie|last=Sefko|title=Mavericks add two-way player McLaughlin|url=https://www.mavs.com/new-player/|website=Mavs.com|date=September 4, 2021|access-date=September 4, 2021}} He was waived by the Mavericks on January 10, 2022, after appearing in four NBA games.{{cite web|first=Eddie|last=Sefko|title=Mavericks keep Pinson, Chriss; waive McLaughlin|url=https://www.mavs.com/mavs-roster-moves/|website=Mavs.com|date=January 10, 2022|access-date=January 10,
